what: Admin Playwright specs expected the 8 seeded products on one page; the shop now holds about 250 products, so 17 of 35 admin tests failed.
why: Specs were written when the table had 8 rows; the shared data grew over the rounds and the spec lookups did not page.
workaround: Added a seek helper that pages to the row; seed and checks use it; typing into generated dialogs verified and retried. Final admin run 35/35.

what: The admin seed spec created a second Footwear category and a duplicate product on a rerun ('Identifier attribute is not unique') because its lookup only read page 1.
why: Seed was not idempotent for rows that sit beyond the first table page.
workaround: Seed now checks existing rows with seek before creating.

what: A duplicate category created by the test seed was removed with a direct SQL DELETE on the Postgres container, outside the model and app.
why: Builder cleaned test debris directly in the database instead of through the app.
workaround: One SQL delete; the category had no products. Reported in the round report.

what: In pw-r16u-q 14 of 15 failures waited 40 s for #kc-form-login. Keycloak looked healthy when checked afterwards (0 restarts, no OOM, 2-10 ms discovery answers, port 8280 not 8080). The builder blamed load from other Docker stacks on the same VM.
why: Root cause not established; the 15 specs passed on rerun (17 passed, 15.3 min) without any change.
workaround: Reran the failing specs serially with -c playwright.local.config.ts; recorded in GAPS R16U-18.

what: Specs with exact counts or stock readings flapped because the reservation job (F73) cancels unpaid orders at any time: F48 expected 97 got 0 in final2, F23 expected 57 got 58 in final6.
why: Shared, time-moving data; the job changes the day counts and stock between two readings.
workaround: F48 and F23 compare direction of change instead of exact sums; one exact stock assertion left in F23 and rerun green. Recorded as GAPS R16U-17, R16U-18, R16U-19.

what: A Playwright run was started without -c playwright.local.config.ts and failed on the missing Chromium build, so that run proved nothing.
why: Forgot the local config that points to the installed Chrome.
workaround: Reran with -c playwright.local.config.ts.

what: Customer spec helper assumed the search box of a cards list is visible at once; cards lists show it a moment later.
why: Card layout renders its search after the page; a table has none.
workaround: Helper waits up to 4 s for the search box before continuing.

what: Other specs failed once on shared data or timing and passed on rerun: F36 coupon message not found, F37 sale price still shown, F44 export filter, F49 click timeout, F63-F66 filter button not found.
why: Shared data (sale windows, coupon states, slow pages under Docker load); causes not isolated.
workaround: Reran the named specs; all passed (7 passed in one rerun, F49 alone 1.7 min).

what: Shop tests change seeded product price, stock and names and do not restore them; ensureStock only raises stock.
why: Tests were written against a fresh shop; the shared data was kept across runs.
workaround: None; listed under not done in the round report.

what: Playwright install chromium hangs at extraction on this machine; the local config uses the installed Google Chrome channel and no retries.
why: Environment problem of the builder machine.
workaround: playwright.local.config.ts override (channel chrome, workers 1, retries 0).

what: The kb read-discipline guard repeatedly printed '[kb] Repeated source searching, still no kb consult' and '3 consecutive searches without consulting the knowledge base' (about 40 times) while the builder ran source greps and test commands. The nudges did not lead to a kb_search.
why: Guard counts shell and grep calls on generated code as source searching, so bulk test work triggers it.
workaround: Ignored the nudges; continued with grep and test runs.

what: Docker Desktop VM disk went read-only during a long Playwright run; Docker Desktop was restarted and Postgres recovered (602 orders afterwards).
why: Docker VM disk filled during the long runs on the shared machine.
workaround: Restarted Docker Desktop and Postgres; data kept.

what: kb_get on the cards-container blueprint returned only the intro line, so the builder read the catalog files from disk.
why: kb_get without a section returns the first section only, and the blueprint's useful sections were not reachable that way.
workaround: Read BLUEPRINT.md and frontend.md from disk (GAPS R16U-1).

what: A cards container placed inside a view fails with 'fetch is not a function', and the relation proxy gets no refresh counter.
why: Custom relation lists read through the generated service; the cards container path is not wired for that case.
workaround: Relation lists built as custom elements that read through the generated service.

what: The cards container shows no table operations, loading state or empty state; the hook has to add the action bar, loading and empty states itself.
why: The catalog describes the cards hook as a table replacement but does not list what the table adds.
workaround: Hook adds toolbar, action bar and empty state; shared ListBars.tsx.

what: A detail view cannot be replaced as a whole, so every field of the order, quote, sale, return, wallet, seller, company and notification detail needed its own custom element (93 field elements).
why: Custom visual element extension point works per field, not per view.
workaround: Custom detail layouts built per field element with DetailLayout.

what: Company pages take 4 to 9 seconds with the shared data; the specs wait up to 45 s and the company pages are still slow.
why: Model performance with this data volume (company relations).
workaround: Specs tolerate the delay; no fix.

what: Top-bar group titles are not translated in the Hungarian UI, and the new Hungarian labels come from the translation script and have not been reviewed by a person.
why: Group titles are not in the translation map.
workaround: None; listed under not done.

what: Profile form, all operation input forms, the shop settings view and admin plain CRUD tables stay generated; only lists and detail views were converted.
why: Editing forms need the generated validation and error messages; plain CRUD tables are not in the custom UI rule.

what: Admin specs fixed (seek helper, idempotent seed, verified typing); 35 of 35 admin tests passed in the last full run.
why: Spec and seed fixes, no product change.

what: Customer specs fixed and made tolerant of shared data (F23, F48, F49); final customer runs 78/78 and 77/78, then F23 rerun green.
why: Test changes only.

what: Two kb_get calls with a path only (scheduled-data-sync-pipeline and external-system-staging-entity) returned the intro section and '(+7 more sections)'; the builder then read the same catalog files from disk with read and grep.
why: kb_get without a section gives the first section only; the builder did not pass a section from kb_search.
workaround: Read the files from disk.

what: The email search did not surface the Email Service section of agent-docs; the builder then wrote that agent-docs do not describe the EmailService API and checked the jar with javap.
why: kb_search on email and Handlebars returned blueprint and practice pages, not agent-docs/backend/platform-behavior-reference.agent.md 'Email Service'.
workaround: javap on osgi-email-api jar and unpacked impl class.

what: best-practices/backend/email-service-integration.md says the agent-docs do not describe the EmailService API. agent-docs/backend/platform-behavior-reference.agent.md has an 'Email Service' section with sendMessage(EmailMessage.emailBuilder()), the fields, attachments, inline content and the IllegalArgumentException for an invalid address.
why: The practice page was written before the agent-doc section existed or was not updated.
workaround: Used the agent-doc section (as found by the builder via javap).

what: Compile against the platform e-mail API needs osgi-email-api as a provided dependency; the builder added it to generator-overrides/app/pom.xml.extra-dependencies.fragment.hbs and to the order-tests pom, the same way F39 added handlebars.
why: The e-mail API bundle is in the Karaf runtime and not in the generated app pom; the catalog does not say how to compile against it.
workaround: Provided-scope dependency in the generator-overrides fragment and order-tests pom.

what: Mail rows failed with 'The platform mail service is not available.' after switching to SMTP localhost:1025 (log SMTP server off). Karaf log showed the osgi-email bundles started; JavaMailSenderActivator is configuration-policy=require. The builder added SMTP user and password and restarted; the root cause was not confirmed in the chunk.
why: Unknown. kb says the mail service (JavaMailSenderActivator) is created only when the log SMTP server is off; the builder checked the config templates.
workaround: Added JUDO_PLATFORM_MAIL_SMTP_USER and PASSWORD to judo-karaf.env and restarted; F77 spec still open at chunk end.

what: Startup log at ERROR: LiquibaseModelDataSourcePrehook 'Could not find compatible schema model' with NoClassDefFoundError for hu/blackbelt/epsilon/runtime/execution/contexts/EolExecutionContext after schema-upgrade. The builder filtered these lines out of its checks and did not follow them up.
why: Missing epsilon runtime class in the Karaf runtime; cause not investigated.
workaround: None; filtered out of the health check.

what: The generated admin menu items for the new entities were named after the entity (CarrierEventInfo, MailTemplateInfo, OutgoingMailInfo, ImportRunInfo); the spec looked for 'Mail templates'. The builder relabelled the four menu items with the CLI.
why: Menu labels default to the entity name; the builder did not set labels when adding the entities.
workaround: judo update webshop::Admin::Menu_19..22 -s label=...

what: The builder did not call kb_search before writing the F76-F79 code (only kb_get at L8839 and L9043, kb_search at L8837, L8953, L9041). It used grep on generated SDK sources and javap for API shapes, although the round rule asked for one kb call per function.
why: Work moved quickly through generated code and the kb guard nudges; the kb was not consulted per function.
workaround: Some API facts were taken from the generated sources.

what: Several small tool mistakes: a sed call with a bad argument, javap with the wrong nested class name, psql -c with \dt, mvn -pl order-tests (reactor error), 'timeout' missing on macOS, git add of ignored .scratch files, a sed -i without the macOS suffix.
why: Builder typing and shell habits on macOS.
workaround: Fixed in the next command.

what: Java compile errors in the new services: getters of optional attributes return Optional (getMailProvider, getCarrierProvider), BooleanFilter has no equalTo (isTrue and isFalse exist), and OrderMails was not imported. Fixed in one cycle.
why: Builder assumed plain getters and an equalTo filter; the Optional return shape and the BooleanFilter API are generated facts.
workaround: Used orElse, isFalse(), and the import.

what: Frontend model build printed many 'XMI ID COLLISION DETECTED' errors for TabularReferenceField link actions (Admin model) after the new admin cards. The head of the output was checked; the BUILD result of that run was not read.
why: Unknown; possibly the new admin tables or the translation step.
workaround: None recorded.

what: The Level 9b integration suite took 158 s for 19 tests and printed large SQL traces; the builder read the surefire report instead.
why: Heavy aggregate queries in the test kit and HSQLDB logging.
workaround: Read surefire report.

what: Catalog path check for the abandoned-cart reminder: the builder read osgi-scheduled-background-jobs from disk and then wrote its own cart touch and reminder marker; no kb call for F78 is in the chunk.
why: Same as the general kb skip above.
workaround: Read blueprint from disk.

what: CLI: 'judo update <BinaryType> --add mimeTypes=X' does not add a second MIME type; the schema keeps only the first value. 'update -s mimeTypes=a,b' also keeps only the first. 'query esm BinaryType --select mimeTypes' needs a subselection.
why: Multi-value MIME list not handled by --add or -s in this CLI build.
workaround: One BinaryType per format: CsvDocument (text/csv) and JsonDocument (application/json).

what: CLI: 'judo create -t MimeType -n json' fails with 'name not defined for MimeTypeCreateInput'. judo-cli.agent.md line 95 says MimeType has no name (type and subType). The builder found it by trial and by grep on disk, not by kb.
why: MimeType create takes type and subType (DEDICATED route addMimeType).
workaround: create -t MimeType --ns webshop -s type=application -s subType=json

what: CLI: 'validate --strict' failed after 'fill' of ImportRunInfo with 'NamedElementHaveToBeInApplication ... startImport::FormCall'. Deleting the OperationForm did not clear it; deleting the TableOperation did, and re-adding the operation with 'update <Table> --add feature --feature startImport --as tableAction' passed.
why: Orphan form call left behind by fill after an operation was created on a table.
workaround: Delete the table operation, re-add with --add feature --as tableAction.

what: CLI: 'judo query ui Form' and 'query ui Action' with grep returned no generated form FQNs for the new operations; the builder had to infer names from Table output.
why: Query result for forms is empty or the FQN shape differs from the grep pattern.
workaround: Inferred names from Table and Action output.

what: CLI: 'judo query <Type>' with -m given fails with 'Missing required parameter <typeName>'; the model name has to be a positional 'esm' argument. The usage text does not make this clear.
why: Builder passed -m and then the type, without the model positional.
workaround: Used query esm <Type> --select fqn.

what: CLI: 'judo generate' removes target/judo-cli.jar and the CLI is missing until './judo.sh generate-root' is run.
why: generate cleans target; the rule says re-fetch the jar after generate.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh generate-root.

what: Frontend admin screens for the new entities: CLI representationComponent=card on OutgoingMailInfo and ImportRunInfo tables worked; the generated hook keys exist after generate.
why: Worked as documented; noted for the catalog check.

what: The scheduled work is an OSGi scheduler (ShopScheduler and ReservationJob, own executor) that calls modeled static operations (ShopJobs: releaseExpired, syncCarrier, sendMails, remindCarts, processImport) through the Dispatcher, so each runs in a transaction. The admin buttons run the same work with an optional minutes input, so tests never sleep.
why: Platform has no scheduler; the agent-docs Scheduled Work section says to use Dispatcher.callOperation for modeled ops.

what: Order mails are sent by an OrderMails post-call trigger from each operation that changes an order, not by interceptors, because interceptors do not run around custom operations.
why: catalog platform-email-template-service says interceptors fire only on built-in operations.

what: Carrier and mail are stubs behind one interface each, switched by shop settings (STUB_SUCCEED, STUB_FAIL, STUB_TIMEOUT). The timeout stub throws at once and nothing sleeps.
why: Pattern from the external API adapter practice; tests need succeed, fail and timeout.

what: Local mail: a Mailpit container on port 1025 and judo-karaf.env SMTP variables; JUDO_PLATFORM_LOG_SMTP_SERVER set to false.
why: Catalog says for local testing point SMTP at localhost:1025 in judo-karaf.env.

what: Adding to the cart resets the reminder marker (cartReminderSentAt) so that a new quiet period starts; the reminder job sends at most one mail per cart.
why: A reminder belongs to the old cart content.

what: The builder says the app bundle has no JSON library, so it wrote a small MiniJson reader for the flat array of objects. The Karaf feature list it printed includes jackson-features.
why: Unverified claim; the bulk JSON practice does not say which library the runtime provides.
workaround: Custom MiniJson.java reader (about 100 lines).

what: Carrier integration: CarrierAdapter stubs, CarrierService, CarrierSyncService, CarrierEvent staging entity, SyncCarrier job, shop setting for the carrier provider, tracking number and carrier status on the shipment card (customer). Build passes; screenshots and specs not finished in the chunk.
why: Built in the R17 Level 9b work.

what: Transactional mail: MailService with templates (MailTemplate), OutgoingMail outbox, OrderMails trigger, SendMails job, admin Sent mails and Mail templates screens (cards). Build passes; the F77 smoke spec was still failing at chunk end (mail row error, see the platform mail issue).
why: Built in the R17 Level 9b work.

what: Abandoned-cart reminder: CartReminderService, touch() in CartService.add, RemindCarts job, cart reminder settings, mail template for the reminder. Build passes; spec not run in the chunk.
why: Built in the R17 Level 9b work.

what: Product import: ImportRun and ImportRowError entities, BulkImportInput with CSV and JSON file types (two BinaryTypes), ImportService, MiniJson reader, admin Import runs cards (A8) with Undo, scripts/gen-import-products.py for 5 000 rows with 10 bad rows. Build passes; the 5 000-row run was not done in the chunk.
why: Built in the R17 Level 9b work.
